The '''2026 United States Senate special election in Ohio''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the state of [[Ohio]]. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] appointee [[Jon Husted]] and [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] former senator [[Sherrod Brown]] are the respective nominees for their parties. The winner will complete the term won in [[2022 United States Senate election in Ohio|2022]] by [[JD Vance]], who resigned in 2025 to become vice president.

Seeking to keep the seat after his appointment, Husted ran unopposed for the Republican nomination. Brown, who represented Ohio in the Senate for three terms until his defeat in [[2024 United States Senate election in Ohio|2024]], won the Democratic nomination against minimal opposition.

This will be the first U.S. Senate special election in Ohio since [[1954 United States Senate special election in Ohio|1954]].

== Background ==
After voting for [[President Barack Obama]] in both [[2008 United States presidential election in Ohio|2008]] and [[2012 United States presidential election in Ohio|2012]], Ohio has trended increasingly Republican in subsequent years and is now considered a moderate to strong [[Red states and blue states|red state]] at the federal and state level. Republicans control all statewide offices, majorities in both chambers of the [[Ohio State Legislature|state legislature]], and hold both [[United States Senate|Senate]] seats. Republicans also have a majority of the state's [[United States House of Representatives|House]] delegation with ten seats compared to five for Democrats.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Grabar|first=Henry|date=November 13, 2018|title=Democrats Proved They Can Win Again in Michigan, Wisconsin, and Pennsylvania. Why Not Ohio?|url=https://slate.com/business/2018/11/why-ohio-may-not-swing-state.html|access-date=January 18, 2026|website=Slate Magazine|language=en}}</ref>

Republican nominee [[Donald Trump]] won Ohio in [[2016 United States presidential election in Ohio|2016]] and [[2020 United States presidential election in Ohio|2020]] by 8 percentage points, and in [[2024 United States presidential election in Ohio|2024]] grew his margin to 11 percentage points.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schladen |first=Marty |date=2024-11-06 |title=Trump wins Ohio for a third time |url=https://ohiocapitaljournal.com/2024/11/05/trump-wins-ohio-for-a-third-time-associated-press-projects/ |access-date=2024-12-05 |website=[[Ohio Capital Journal]] |language=en-US}}</ref> Additionally, Republican [[JD Vance]], now the [[Vice President of the United States|vice president of the United States]], defeated Democrat [[Tim Ryan (Ohio politician)|Tim Ryan]] in the [[2022 United States Senate election in Ohio|2022 U.S. Senate election]] by slightly over 6 points, while Republican [[Bernie Moreno]] defeated then-incumbent Sherrod Brown in the [[2024 United States Senate election in Ohio|2024 U.S. Senate election]] by slightly over 3.5 points.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Evans |first=Nick |date=2024-11-06 |title=Republican Bernie Moreno defeats incumbent Sherrod Brown for Ohio U.S. Senate seat • Ohio Capital Journal |url=https://ohiocapitaljournal.com/2024/11/05/republican-bernie-moreno-defeats-incumbent-sherrod-brown-for-ohio-u-s-senate-seat-ap-projects/ |access-date=2024-12-05 |website=[[Ohio Capital Journal]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Interim appointment==
According to Ohio law, if a U.S. Senate seat becomes vacant, the [[List of governors of Ohio|governor]] appoints a replacement who serves until December 15 following the next regularly scheduled statewide election that occurs more than 180 days after the vacancy. A special election to fill the remainder of the term is then held concurrently with that regular state election, which in this case would be the one on [[2026 Ohio elections|November 3, 2026]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Burd |first1=Aaron |title=How J.D. Vance's replacement in U.S. Senate will be picked if he becomes vice president |url=https://www.nbc4i.com/news/your-local-election-hq/how-j-d-vances-replacement-in-u-s-senate-will-be-picked-if-he-becomes-vice-president/ |work=[[WCMH-TV]] |date=July 16, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Filling vacancies in elective offices |url=https://www.ohiosos.gov/globalassets/elections/eoresources/general/fillingvacancies.pdf |publisher=Ohio Secretary of State |access-date=November 6, 2024 |page=2}}</ref> Governor [[Mike DeWine]] chose then-Lieutenant Governor Jon Husted to replace Vance in the Senate.

== General election ==
Data centers have become a major issue in the campaign, and a poll from [[Bowling Green State University]] showed 71% of Ohioans support a temporary ban on new construction of data centers. Brown has criticized Husted for his support of data centers in the past. As lieutenant governor from 2019 to 2025, Husted backed millions of dollars in tax breaks for data center construction projects in Ohio. Husted has defended data centers, saying they bring new jobs and money to rural areas. Husted has described data centers as a "local issue", and Brown has said that the approval of data centers should be decided on the local level.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sivaraman |first=Siddarth |date=August 10, 2026 |title=Ohio U.S. Senate candidates offer contrasting visions for data centers |url=https://ohiocapitaljournal.com/2026/08/10/ohio-u-s-senate-candidates-offer-contrasting-visions-for-data-centers/ |access-date=September 29, 2026 |website=Ohio Capital Journal |language=en-US}}</ref>

A September 2026 poll conducted by Bowling Green State University found that 25% of likely Ohio voters incorrectly believed Sherrod Brown was the incumbent U.S. senator from the state, despite him having lost re-election in 2024.<ref>{{cite news|last=Davines|first=Emily|date=September 28, 2026|title=In Ohio, a Humbling Question for Senator Jon Husted: Are You the Incumbent?|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/28/us/politics/john-husted-ohio-president-trump-midterms.html|url-access=subscription|work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref>

The '''2026 United States Senate election in Oklahoma''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate|U.S. Senate]] to represent the state of [[Oklahoma]]. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] congressman [[Kevin Hern]] and [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] nurse N'Kiyla Jasmine Thomas are the nominees for their respective parties. Republican appointee [[Alan Armstrong]], who was named to the seat in March after [[Markwayne Mullin]] resigned to become [[United States Secretary of Homeland Security|secretary of homeland security]], is prohibited by Oklahoma law from seeking a full term.

Primary elections were held on June 16. Hern, endorsed by President [[Donald Trump]], won the Republican nomination with 69.8% of the vote over country singer [[Ty England]]. No candidate received a majority in the Democratic primary; Thomas defeated attorney Jim Priest in the August 25 runoff with 61.2% of the vote.

Democrats have not won a Senate election in Oklahoma since [[1990 United States Senate election in Oklahoma|1990]].

==Background==
A United States Senate election in Oklahoma is scheduled to be held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the U.S. Senate to represent the state of [[Oklahoma]]. [[Primary election]]s took place on June 16 with [[runoff election]]s on August 25 in races where no candidate received over 50 percent of the vote in June. The candidate filing deadline was April 3.<ref name="Ballotpedia">{{cite web |title=United States Senate election in Oklahoma, 2026 |url=https://ballotpedia.org/United_States_Senate_election_in_Oklahoma,_2026 |website=ballotpedia.org |publisher=[[Ballotpedia]] |access-date=November 12, 2024 |language=en}}</ref> If only one candidate files for a party's nomination, they are declared the nominee.<ref>{{cite web |title=26 O.S. 6-102 |url=https://www.oscn.net/applications/oscn/DeliverDocument.asp?CiteID=78518 |website=oscn.net |publisher=[[Oklahoma State Courts Network]] |access-date=April 5, 2026}}</ref> 

The seat was originally held by [[Jim Inhofe]], who was last elected in [[2020 United States Senate election in Oklahoma|2020]]. Two years later, in 2022, then-Congressman [[Markwayne Mullin]] won a special election to finish Inhofe's term after Inhofe had announced his resignation at the end of the [[117th United States Congress|117th Congress]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Casteel |first1=Chris |title=Markwayne Mullin defeats Kendra Horn in Oklahoma US Senate race |url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/news/politics/elections/state/2022/11/09/republican-markwayne-mullin-wins-race-to-replace-sen-jim-inhofe/69611629007/ |access-date=March 8, 2026 |work=[[The Oklahoman]] |date=November 8, 2022}}</ref> After [[Donald Trump]] won the [[2024 United States presidential election]], Mullin was rumored as a contender for [[U.S. Secretary of the Interior|secretary of the interior]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Liese |first1=Sarah |last2=Hallum |first2=Katie |title=Oklahoma Sen. Markwayne Mullin reportedly in running for Trump cabinet post |url=https://www.kgou.org/politics-and-government/2024-11-12/oklahoma-sen-markwayne-mullin-reportedly-in-running-for-trump-cabinet-post |access-date=November 12, 2024 |work=[[KGOU]] |date=November 12, 2024 |language=en}}</ref> Mullin's resignation would have affected the [[2026 Oklahoma gubernatorial election|gubernatorial election]], as governor [[Kevin Stitt]] would have appointed a replacement who must sign a potentially unenforceable{{efn|While state law requires the appointee to sign an oath promising not to run for the following term, federal law may prevent its enforcement. The oath could lead to litigation if an appointee challenges the law.<ref name="Mullin speculation" />}} oath promising not to run for reelection in 2026.<ref name="Mullin speculation">{{cite news |last1=Savage |first1=Tres |last2=Brinkman |first2=Bennett |title=Domino scenarios: Sen. Markwayne Mullin Cabinet rumor spurs speculation |url=https://nondoc.com/2024/11/12/markwayne-mullin-cabinet-rumor-spurs-speculation/ |access-date=November 12, 2024 |work=NonDoc |date=12 November 2024}}</ref> Mullin was ultimately not nominated as the secretary of interior.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Wahpekeche |first1=Dacoda |title=Sen. Markwayne Mullin talks possibly being in Donald Trump's Cabinet |url=https://www.koco.com/article/oklahoma-markwayne-mullin-donald-trump-cabinet-possibility/62910530 |access-date=November 16, 2024 |work=[[KOCO]] |date=November 15, 2024 |language=en}}</ref> However, in March 2026, Mullin was named as Trump's pick to replace [[United States Secretary of Homeland Security|secretary of homeland security]] [[Kristi Noem]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Noem out, Trump picks Mullin as DHS secretary |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/03/05/markwayne-mullin-noem-dhs-00814761 |website=POLITICO |access-date=7 March 2026 |language=en |date=5 March 2026}}</ref> and was confirmed on March 23, 2026.<ref name=":4">{{Cite news |last=Bustillo |first=Ximena |date=2026-03-23 |title=Markwayne Mullin confirmed as the next secretary of Homeland Security |url=https://www.npr.org/2026/03/23/g-s1-114813/markwayne-mullin-confirmed-homeland-security |access-date=2026-03-24 |work=NPR |language=en}}</ref>

== Interim appointment ==
Mullin was confirmed as the [[United States Secretary of Homeland Security|secretary of homeland security]]<ref name=":4" /> and resigned as senator on March 23, 2026. Governor [[Kevin Stitt]] was required to appoint a replacement within 30 days. He stated the appointee would serve the remainder of the current term until January 3, 2027, though state law provides that the appointment lasts only until the November election is certified by the [[Oklahoma State Election Board]].<ref name="Oklahoman-3.7.26" /> The interim appointee must have been a registered Republican for the past five years,<ref name="shakes">{{cite web |title=Appointment of Mullin shakes up 2026 Oklahoma elections |url=https://www.kgou.org/show/capitol-insider/2026-03-06/appointment-of-mullin-shakes-up-2026-oklahoma-elections |website=KGOU NPR |access-date=8 March 2026 |language=en}}</ref> and they would have to sign an oath stating they will not run in the 2026 election.<ref name="NextA">{{cite web |last1=Ramos |first1=Lionel |title=Markwayne Mullin tapped to lead Homeland Security. Here's what happens to his Senate seat |url=https://www.kosu.org/whats-next-after-mullin |website=KOSU |access-date=8 March 2026 |language=en |date=5 March 2026}}</ref> On March 24, 2026, Governor Stitt announced that oil and gas executive [[Alan Armstrong]] would replace Mullin; Armstrong was sworn in by senator [[Chuck Grassley]] later that day.<ref name="PoliticoSenate">{{cite web |last=Svirnovskiy|first=Gregory|title=Stitt picks energy executive Alan Armstrong as next Oklahoma senator|url=https://www.politico.com/live-updates/2026/03/24/congress/oklahoma-senator-alan-armstrong-00841481|website=[[Politico]]|access-date=2026-03-24|language=en-US|date=2026-03-24}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Carney|first=Jordan|title=Introducing Sen. Alan Armstrong|url=https://www.politico.com/live-updates/2026/03/24/congress/senator-alan-armstrong-00842118|website=[[Politico]]|access-date=2026-03-24|language=en-US|date=2026-03-24}}</ref>

The '''2026 United States Senate election in''' '''Oregon''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the state of [[Oregon]]. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] incumbent [[Jeff Merkley]] is seeking a fourth term.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.opb.org/article/2025/07/10/jeff-merkley-seeking-4th-term/|title=Oregon’s Jeff Merkley will seek a 4th term in US Senate, ending speculation|last=VanderHart|first=Dirk|publisher=[[Oregon Public Broadcasting]]|access-date=July 11, 2025|date=July 11, 2025}}</ref> He is being challenged by [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] state senator [[David Brock Smith]].<ref name="Smith Wins">{{cite web|last=Rush|first=Claire|date=May 22, 2026|title=David Brock Smith wins GOP primary for US Senate in Oregon, will face Democratic incumbent Merkley|url=https://apnews.com/article/oregon-primary-election-2026-republican-senate-32d9f95d985f971380476246c6f6b723|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260523193932/https://apnews.com/article/oregon-primary-election-2026-republican-senate-32d9f95d985f971380476246c6f6b723|archive-date=May 23, 2026|url-status=live|access-date=May 23, 2026|work=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref>

In the Democratic primary, Merkley was nominated with 93.2% of the vote against minimal opposition. Smith won the Republican nomination with 29.5% of the vote over former Linn County party chair [[Jo Rae Perkins]] and real estate broker Brent Barker.

Republicans have not won a Senate election in Oregon since [[2002 United States Senate election in Oregon|2002]].

The '''2026 United States Senate election in South Carolina''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent [[South Carolina]]. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] appointee [[Darline Graham]] and [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] pediatrician [[Annie Andrews (pediatrician)|Annie Andrews]] are the nominees for their respective parties.

Graham's brother, four-term incumbent [[Lindsey Graham|Lindsey]], won the Republican nomination in the June 9 primaries, but died on July 11. Appointed to her brother's seat and encouraged to run with the support of President [[Donald Trump]], Graham defeated congressman [[Ralph Norman]] in a runoff on August 25 with 52.5% of the vote after no candidate received a majority in an August 11 special primary. Andrews won the Democratic nomination with 61.5% of the vote over former [[Paine College]] administrator Brandon Brown.

The winner is expected<!--Do not change. Stating definitively in [[Wikipedia:Wikivoice|Wikivoice]] that the winner will be female is inappropriate. --> to be the first woman elected to the Senate from South Carolina. Democrats have not won a Senate election in the state since [[1998 United States Senate election in South Carolina|1998]].

== Background ==
South Carolina is generally considered a [[Red states and blue states|Republican stronghold]], having last elected a [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrat]] to the U.S. Senate in [[1998 United States Senate election in South Carolina|1998]]. Republican nominee [[Donald Trump]] won South Carolina in the [[2020 United States presidential election in South Carolina|2020 presidential election]] by 12 percentage points; in [[2024 United States presidential election in South Carolina|2024]], his margin grew to 18 points. Republicans control every statewide office (except the [[South Carolina Comptroller General|state's comptroller office]]) and have supermajorities in both chambers of the [[South Carolina State Legislature|state legislature]], both [[United States Senate|U.S. Senate]] seats, and all but one seat in South Carolina's [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. House]] [[South Carolina's congressional delegations|congressional delegation]].<ref>{{Cite web |first1=Abraham |last1=Kenmore |first2=Seanna |last2=Adcox |date=November 6, 2024 |title=Trump wins SC for 3rd time, on his way to stunning White House victory |url=https://scdailygazette.com/2024/11/05/trump-wins-sc-for-3rd-consecutive-presidential-contest/ |access-date=December 21, 2024 |website=South Carolina Daily Gazette |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |first1=Jessica |last1=Holdman |first2=Abraham |last2=Kenmore |date=November 6, 2024 |title=SC Republicans celebrate red wave that gives GOP biggest advantage in 150 years |url=https://scdailygazette.com/2024/11/06/sc-republicans-celebrates-red-wave-that-gives-gop-strongest/ |access-date=December 7, 2024 |website=South Carolina Daily Gazette |language=en-US}}</ref>

Lindsey Graham was first elected in [[2002 United States Senate election in South Carolina|2002]], defeating Democrat [[Alex Sanders (politician)|Alex Sanders]] by about 10 percentage points. He was reelected in [[2008 United States Senate election in South Carolina|2008]], [[2014 United States Senate election in South Carolina|2014]], and most recently in [[2020 United States Senate election in South Carolina|2020]], defeating [[Jaime Harrison]] by 10 percentage points in what was expected to be a [[dead heat]].<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Lobosco |first1=Katie |date=November 4, 2020 |title=Lindsey Graham defeats Jaime Harrison in South Carolina |url=https://www.cnn.com/2020/11/03/politics/south-carolina-senate-race-2020/index.html |access-date=December 21, 2024 |publisher=CNN |language=en}}</ref> In January 2025, he declared that he was running for reelection.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Connaughton |first1=Kevin |date=January 14, 2025 |title=Lindsey Graham announces campaign team, funding for 2026 re-election bid |url=https://www.wistv.com/2025/01/14/lindsey-graham-announces-campaign-team-funding-2026-re-election-bid/ |access-date=June 17, 2025 |publisher=WIS-TV |language=en}}</ref> Graham died suddenly on July 11, 2026, of [[cardiac arrest]].<ref name="Cardiac">{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/politics-news/sen-lindsey-graham-dies-71-brief-sudden-illness-rcna552722 |title=Sen. Lindsey Graham dies at 71 after 'brief and sudden illness' |website=NBC News |last1=Wong |first1=Scott |last2=Thorp V |first2=Frank |date=July 12, 2026 |access-date=July 12, 2026}}</ref>

==Special Republican primary==
Lindsey Graham, who had won the Republican primary, died on July 11, 2026. Under South Carolina law, a special primary election was held on August 11 to select a replacement Republican nominee.<ref name="Justia">{{cite web |title=2025 South Carolina Code of Laws Title 7 - Elections Chapter 11 - Designation And Nomination Of Candidates Section 7-11-55. Substitution of candidates when nominee selected by primary election |url=https://law.justia.com/codes/south-carolina/title-7/chapter-11/section-7-11-55/|website=Justicia|access-date=July 11, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title= Title 7 - Elections CHAPTER 11 Designation and Nomination of Candidates ARTICLE 1 Methods of Nomination |url= https://www.scstatehouse.gov/Archives/CodeofLaws2023/t07c011.php |website= South Carolina Code of Laws |access-date= July 12, 2026}}</ref>

The three-week campaign was an unusually compressed U.S. Senate race.<ref>{{Cite web |date= July 13, 2026 |title= Graham Senate Seat Special Election: The Aug. 11 Primary – Democrats organized to vote with light turnout projected |url= https://myrtlebeachsc.com/graham-senate-seat-special-election/ |access-date= July 28, 2026 |work= Myrtle Beach SC News}}</ref> The candidate filing period opened at noon on July 21 and closed at noon on July 28.<ref>{{Cite web |last1= Bain |first1= Sydni |date= July 13, 2026 |title= U.S. Senate Special Republican Party Filing & Primary |url= https://scvotes.gov/u-s-senate-special-republican-party-filing-primary/ |access-date= July 27, 2026 |website= SC Votes - South Carolina Election Commission |language= en-US}}</ref> The South Carolina State Election Commission ruled that the special Republican primary will be treated as a continuation of the June 9 primary. Accordingly, only voters who participated in the Republican primary or did not vote in either party's June 9 primary were eligible to vote; those who voted in the Democratic primary were ineligible, despite South Carolina's open primary system, which does not require party registration.<ref>{{Cite web |last1= Moore |first1= Stephanie |date= July 13, 2026 |title= South Carolina to hold special primary for Lindsey Graham's Senate seat |url= https://www.wyff4.com/article/south-carolina-special-primary-lindsey-graham-seat/71917010 |website= WYFF}}</ref> Federal law generally requires military and overseas ballots to be mailed at least 45 days before a federal election, while the special election took take place 31 days after Lindsey Graham's death triggered the vacancy.<ref>{{Cite web |last1= Wooten |first1= Alan |date= July 13, 2026 |title= Voters will choose Graham's successor on ballot through primary |url= https://www.thecentersquare.com/south_carolina/article_7446d7ac-09ea-437d-8fc5-efc7ba6e2ac6.html |website= The Center Square}}</ref> 

In June, the South Carolina Republican Party adopted a measure stating that to qualify for elected office in a Republican primary, a candidate must have voted in at least two of the last three statewide Republican primary elections.<ref>{{cite web |title= The Rules of the South Carolina Republican Party |url= https://sc.gop/wp-content/uploads/sites/14/2026/07/SCGOPRules2026.pdf |website= SC GOP |access-date= July 30, 2026}}</ref> On July 28, the South Carolina Republican Party decertified three candidates seeking the nomination. Clark Neilson was disqualified for not living in the state and Darius Mitchell and Danny Ford II were disqualified for not meeting the new state party requirement.<ref name= "Disqualified" /> On July 30, Ford announced that he was suing the South Carolina Republican party to be placed on the ballot. His attorney, state senator [[Brad Hutto]], said the party's new rule violates both the South Carolina and the US constitutions.<ref>{{Cite web |last1= Reynolds |first1= Nick |date= July 30, 2026 |title= Danny Ford II, disqualified from the Republican US Senate race, sues SCGOP for ballot access |url= https://www.postandcourier.com/politics/danny-ford-scgop-senate-republican/article_243f2d3a-384f-4414-aadc-e830e41946ec.html |access-date= July 30, 2026 |website= [[The Post and Courier]]}}</ref> On August 3, [[Richland County, South Carolina|Richland County]] judge Daniel Coble ordered that Ford's name be on the ballot.<ref>{{Cite web |last1= Biddix |first1= Stephen| last2= Kesler |first2= Alex| last3= Hemphill |first3= Joshua |date= August 4, 2026 |title= Judge rules Danny Ford II must appear on SC Senate primary ballot ahead of early voting |url= https://www.wistv.com/2026/08/04/judge-rules-danny-ford-ii-must-appear-senate-primary-ballot/ |access-date= August 5, 2026 |website= [[WIS (TV)]] |language= en}}</ref>

U.S. President [[Donald Trump]] said that if she ran in the primary he would endorse [[Darline Graham]], Lindsey Graham's sister.<ref name="politicojune17">{{cite web| url= https://www.politico.com/news/2026/07/17/trump-endorses-darline-graham-for-lindsay-grahams-open-senate-seat-01003457| title= Trump endorses Darline Graham for Lindsey Graham's open Senate seat| last1= Johansen|first1= Ben| website= [[Politico]]| date= June 17, 2026}}</ref> By July 20, she announced she would run in the special primary for a full term. [[Ralph Norman]], [[Russell Fry]], [[Mark Sanford]], and Mark Lynch also launched campaigns.<ref>{{cite web| url= https://apnews.com/article/south-carolina-special-primary-senate-lindsey-graham-666830ac225c8dbf1027d041d9e88b31| title= AP Decision Notes: What to expect in South Carolina's special primary to replace Sen. Lindsey Graham| date= August 10, 2026| website= [[Associated Press]]| last1= Yoon|first1=Robert}}</ref> No candidate received a majority of the vote, so a runoff election between [[Darline Graham]] and [[Ralph Norman]] was held on August 25.<ref>{{Cite web |date= August 25, 2026 |title= Sen. Darline Graham wins the Republican Senate primary runoff in South Carolina |url= https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/darline-graham-winner-south-carolina-gop-senate-primary-rcna593581 |access-date= August 25, 2026 |website= NBC News| last1= Wong| first1= Scott}}</ref>

===Runoff===
Graham and Norman were considered closely matched in the primary, with Graham's endorsement by Trump weighing against Norman's legislative experience and reputation as a staunchly conservative outsider.<ref name= "PBS">{{cite web| url= https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/darline-graham-ralph-norman-go-head-to-head-in-south-carolinas-gop-senate-runoff |title= Darline Graham, Ralph Norman go head-to-head in South Carolina's GOP Senate runoff |website= PBS |last1= Kinnard |first1= Meg |agency= Associated Press |date= August 25, 2026 |access-date= August 27, 2026}}</ref> Trump vigorously campaigned for Graham, headlining a rally for her in [[Myrtle Beach]].<ref name= "DarlineWins">{{cite web| url= https://www.politico.com/news/2026/08/25/darline-graham-wins-south-carolina-senate-runoff-01050320 |title= Political newcomer Darline Graham wins South Carolina's GOP Senate runoff |website= Politico |last1= Hernandez |first1= Alec |date= August 25, 2026 |access-date= August 27, 2026}}</ref> He also made numerous calls to prominent South Carolina officials to secure their support for Graham, including to Russell Fry, who endorsed her on August 14, and to Governor McMaster, who held a press conference emphasizing his support for her.<ref>{{cite web| url= https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/14/us/politics/russell-fry-darline-graham-south-carolina.html| title= Trump Pressured Russell Fry to Endorse Darline Graham for Senate. So He Did.| date= August 14, 2026| last1= Davies|first1= Emily| website= [[The New York Times]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date= August 24, 2026 |title= Gov. McMaster doubles down on endorsement of Darline Graham ahead of SC Senate runoff |url= https://www.wistv.com/2026/08/24/live-gov-mcmaster-sen-darline-graham-holding-press-conference/ |access-date= August 24, 2026 |website= WIS-TV |language= en}}</ref>

In ''[[The New York Times]]'', Michael Gold wrote that Trump had two main disputes with Norman that solidified his support for Graham: Norman's endorsement of [[Nikki Haley]] for president in [[Nikki Haley 2024 presidential campaign|2024]] and his votes (with other members of the [[House Freedom Caucus]]) against several pieces of legislation Trump supported on the grounds that they contained wasteful government spending. Most notably, Norman had initially refused to vote for Trump's flagship second-term policy, the [[One Big Beautiful Bill Act]], which Graham used as evidence that Norman was insufficiently committed to advancing Trump's agenda.<ref name="Gold">{{cite web| url= https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/24/us/politics/ralph-norman-trump-south-carolina.html |title= With Trump Against Him, Can Ralph Norman Win in South Carolina? |newspaper= The New York Times |last1= Gold |first1= Michael |date= August 24, 2026 |access-date= August 27, 2026}}</ref> Norman campaigned around the state, arguing that he had acted against Trump's wishes only because Trump was insufficiently conservative on government spending.<ref name= "Gold"/><ref>{{cite web |last1= Guzman |first1= Jenna |date= August 24, 2026 |title= Ralph Norman speaks to Horry County voters ahead of runoff election |url= https://www.wmbfnews.com/2026/08/24/ralph-norman-speaks-horry-county-voters-ahead-runoff-election/ |access-date= August 24, 2026 |website= WMBF-TV |language= en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title= Ralph Norman Holds Voter Town Hall in Anderson, SC Ahead of Aug. 25 Primary Runoff |url= https://www.c-span.org/program/campaign-2026/ralph-norman-holds-voter-town-hall-in-anderson-sc-ahead-of-aug-25-primary-runoff/684304 |access-date= August 24, 2026 |website= C-SPAN|language= en-us}}</ref>

He is being challenged by [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] activist [[Marquita Bradshaw]] in a rematch of [[2020 United States Senate election in Tennessee|2020]]. In the August 6 [[primary elections]], Hagerty was unopposed the Republican nomination. Bradshaw won the Democratic nomination over former state party director Maria Brewer with 54.8% of the vote. The '''2026 United States Senate election in Texas''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the state of [[Texas]]. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] state attorney general [[Ken Paxton]] and [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] state representative [[James Talarico]] are the nominees for their respective parties.

Four-term Republican incumbent [[John Cornyn]] sought re-election, but was challenged for the party's nomination by Paxton. After no candidate received a majority in the March 3 primary, Paxton, aided by a late endorsement from President [[Donald Trump]], defeated Cornyn with 63.8% of the vote in a [[two-round system|runoff]] on May 26. Cornyn became the first incumbent senator from Texas to lose renomination since Democrat [[Ralph Yarborough]] in [[1970 United States Senate election in Texas|1970]]. In the Democratic primary, Talarico won the nomination with 52.4% of the vote over congresswoman [[Jasmine Crockett]].

Democrats have not won a Senate election in Texas since [[1988 United States Senate election in Texas|1988]].

{{toclimit|4}}

== Background ==
Texas has been considered a [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]]-leaning state throughout the 21st century.<ref>{{Cite web |title=How Texas came to be dominated by Republicans |url=https://www.axios.com/local/dallas/2024/09/05/texas-republican-party-dominance |last=Rajwani-Dharsi |first=Naheed |website=[[Axios (website)|Axios]] |date=September 5, 2024 |access-date=August 19, 2026 |language=en}}</ref> Democrats have not won a [[U.S. Senate]] election in the state since [[Lloyd Bentsen]] was re-elected in [[1988 United States Senate election in Texas|1988]], and they have not won any statewide election in the state since [[Lieutenant Governor of Texas|lieutenant governor]] [[Bob Bullock]] was re-elected in [[1994 Texas lieutenant gubernatorial election|1994]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 30, 2024 |title=No Democrat has won a statewide office in Texas since 1994 |url=https://www.fox4news.com/election/texas-democrat-statewide-senate-president |access-date=August 19, 2026 |website=FOX 4 |language=en-US}}</ref> Republicans have fully controlled the [[Texas Legislature]] since the [[2002 Texas House of Representatives election|2002 elections]]. Texas's Republican lean has waned in the past decade, with Democrats only narrowly losing the 2018 elections for [[2018 United States Senate election in Texas|U.S. Senate]] and [[2018 Texas Attorney General election|attorney general]], buoyed by gains in the state's suburban areas. More recently, however, Republicans have made substantial gains with the state's [[Hispanic and Latino Americans|Hispanic]] population, particularly in the [[Rio Grande Valley]]. Republican [[Donald Trump]] won the state by nearly 14 [[percentage point]]s in the [[2024 United States presidential election in Texas|2024 presidential election]], while U.S. Senator [[Ted Cruz]] [[2024 United States Senate election in Texas|won re-election]] by over 8 points on the same ballot.{{Citation needed|date=August 2026}}

Incumbent Republican senator [[John Cornyn]] was first elected in [[2002 United States Senate election in Texas|2002]] to succeed fellow Republican [[Phil Gramm]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=National Briefing {{!}} Southwest: Texas: New Senator Sworn In |url=https://timesmachine.nytimes.com/timesmachine/2002/12/03/204200.html |access-date=August 19, 2026 |work=The New York Times |language=en |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> Cornyn had previously served as the state's [[Texas Attorney General|attorney general]], as well as a member of the state's [[Supreme Court of Texas|Supreme Court]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Guo |first=Kayla |date=May 27, 2026 |title=John Cornyn's long political career ends in MAGA uprising |url=https://www.texastribune.org/2026/05/26/john-cornyn-texas-senator-paxton-maga-loss-legacy/ |access-date=August 19, 2026 |website=The Texas Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref> He most recently [[2020 United States Senate election in Texas|won re-election in 2020]] with 53.5% of the vote against Democrat [[M. J. Hegar]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Svitek |first=Patrick |date=November 4, 2020 |title=John Cornyn defeats MJ Hegar to retain Texas' U.S. Senate seat |url=https://www.texastribune.org/2020/11/03/john-cornyn-mj-hegar-texas-senate/ |access-date=August 19, 2026 |website=The Texas Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref> Cornyn has a consistently [[Conservatism|conservative]] voting record in the U.S. Senate, and he is considered part of the Republican establishment due to his long tenure in politics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Texas GOP finally turned on Cornyn |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/05/26/cornyn-senate-career-ends-trump-paxton-00937548 |access-date=August 19, 2026 |website=Politico |language=en}}</ref>

==Republican primary==
[[File:John Cornyn (cropped).jpg|thumb|x170px|Incumbent senator [[John Cornyn]] was defeated in the Republican primary runoff.]]
[[File:Wesley Hunt, official portrait, 118th Congress (cropped).jpg|thumb|x170px|[[U.S. Representative]] [[Wesley Hunt]] finished third in the Republican primary.]]

===Background===
Incumbent senator [[John Cornyn]], who was seeking a fifth term, faced a competitive primary from [[Texas Attorney General|attorney general]] [[Ken Paxton]] which progressed to a runoff after no candidate reached a majority in the first round. The two had clashed publicly since 2022, with Paxton criticizing Cornyn for being insufficiently conservative, particularly over his support for [[Ukraine–United States relations#Russo-Ukrainian War (2014–present)|U.S. aid to Ukraine]], [[DREAM Act]] for [[Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals|DACA]] beneficiaries and playing a leading role in the passage of the [[Bipartisan Safer Communities Act|bipartisan gun safety bill]] after the [[Uvalde school massacre]]. Cornyn, in turn, has highlighted [[Ken Paxton#Legal issues|Paxton's legal troubles]], perceived character flaws and corruption, and his [[Ken Paxton#Impeachment|2023 impeachment]], in which Paxton was impeached by the Republican-controlled [[Texas House of Representatives|Texas House]] before the [[Texas Senate|Senate]] later acquitted him of all charges.<ref name="CP"/><ref>{{Cite web |last=Jacobs |first=Ben |date=May 14, 2025 |title=The Republican Trainwreck of the 2026 Election Cycle |url=https://www.politico.com/news/magazine/2025/05/14/cornyn-paxton-texas-gop-primary-infighting-00346390 |access-date=May 15, 2025 |website=Politico |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=McLaughlin |first=Seth |title=Sen. Cornyn's reelection bid faces more warning signs in new Senate primary poll |url=https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2025/jun/3/sen-john-cornyns-reelection-bid-faces-warning-signs-new-senate/ |access-date=June 5, 2025 |website=The Washington Times |date=June 3, 2025 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Goodman |first=J. David |date=May 30, 2025 |title=Cornyn Calls Primary Fight Against Ken Paxton a 'Test of Character' |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/05/30/us/cornyn-paxton-texas-primary.html |access-date=June 29, 2025 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

The race has been seen as a key contest between the [[Republican Party of Texas|Texas Republican Party]]'s establishment wing and its hardline conservative faction.<ref name="CP">{{Cite news |last=Gans |first=Jared |date=February 9, 2025 |title=7 competitive primaries to watch in 2026 |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5133732-2026-midterm-elections-primaries/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250210030210/https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5133732-2026-midterm-elections-primaries/ |archive-date=February 10, 2025 |access-date=February 13, 2025 |work=The Hill |language=en-US}}</ref> In recent years, insurgent [[Radical right (United States)|hard-right]] candidates have steadily gained ground, often ousting more traditional GOP officials. Polling reflects this divide: Paxton holds a commanding lead among "[[Trumpism|Trump Movement]]" voters, while Cornyn performs better with the smaller group of "[[Reagan coalition|Traditional Republicans]]."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jacobs |first=Ben |date=June 7, 2025 |title='Trump movement' turns on Cornyn, poll finds |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/06/07/john-cornyn-ken-paxton-poll-trump-movement-00393045 |access-date=June 7, 2025 |website=Politico |language=en}}</ref> On May 19, 2026, [[Donald Trump]] describing both Paxton and Cornyn as good friends.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 13, 2025 |title=Trump weighs in on Texas Senate race The election takes place amid efforts by the state Republican Party to restrict its primary to registered members. Legislation to allow closed primaries failed, prompting the party to sue the state, claiming the current law violates the [[First Amendment to the United States Constitution|First Amendment]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schneider |first=Andrew |date=December 29, 2025 |title=Texas GOP faces legal opposition in bid to close state's open primary system |url=https://www.keranews.org/politics/2025-12-29/texas-gop-faces-legal-opposition-in-bid-to-close-states-open-primary-system |access-date=January 15, 2026 |website=KERA News |language=en}}</ref> Despite serving as the state's attorney general, Paxton declined to defend the law in court, drawing criticism from those who argued he would gain electorally from a closed primary.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McCormick |first=Cara Brown |date=October 13, 2025 |title=Paxton Concedes He Has a Conflict of Interest in Texas Primary Lawsuit |url=https://ivn.us/posts/paxton-concedes-he-has-conflict-interest-texas-primary-lawsuit-2025-10-13 |access-date=January 15, 2026 |website=Independent Voter News}}</ref>

Cornyn led Paxton narrowly in the primary election, garnering 42.0% of the vote to Paxton's 40.5%, while Hunt placed a distant third with 13.5% of the vote.<ref name="SoS primary results" /><ref name="NYT011">{{cite web |title=Texas Senate Primary 2026: Live Election Results |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2026/us/elections/results-texas-us-senate-primary.html |website=The New York Times |access-date=March 4, 2026 |date=March 3, 2026}}</ref> Support for Cornyn and Paxton was relatively evenly spread across the state, though Cornyn performed slightly better in urban areas, especially [[Dallas]] and [[Austin, Texas|Austin]], while Paxton performed slightly better in rural areas, particularly in [[East Texas]].<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |last1=Coleman |first1=J. Miles |last2=Kondik |first2=Kyle |date=March 4, 2026 |title=Cornyn Staying Alive is Enough to Keep Texas Senate as Likely Republican |url=https://centerforpolitics.org/crystalball/cornyn-staying-alive-is-enough-to-keep-texas-senate-as-likely-republican/ |access-date=March 12, 2026 |website=Sabato's Crystal Ball |language=en-US}}</ref> Hunt performed slightly better in regions which backed Paxton, suggesting his presence on the ballot hurt Cornyn more than Paxton. Even in Hunt's [[Texas's 38th congressional district|own congressional district]], he came in third with barely over 20% of the vote.<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |last=Coleman |first=J. Miles |date=March 12, 2026 |title=Getting Deeper into Texas and North Carolina's Primaries |url=https://centerforpolitics.org/crystalball/getting-deeper-into-texas-and-north-carolinas-primaries/ |access-date=March 12, 2026 |website=Sabato's Crystal Ball |language=en-US}}</ref>

In the days leading up to the March 3 primary, Paxton suggested he could win outright and avoid a runoff. However, Cornyn overperformed expectations in what ''[[The Texas Tribune]]'' described as a "better-than-expected showing". Rolando Garcia, a member of the [[Republican Party of Texas|State Republican Executive Committee]] who supported Hunt in the primary but planned to back Paxton in the runoff, said the result should alarm the Paxton campaign.<ref name="Svit">{{cite web |last1=Klibanoff |first1=Eleanor |last2=Svitek |first2=Patrick |last3=Downey |first3=Renzo |title=Five takeaways from the March 2026 Texas primaries |url=https://www.texastribune.org/2026/03/04/texas-primaries-2026-takeaways-senate-trump-cornyn-paxton-talarico-congress/ |website=The Texas Tribune |access-date=March 4, 2026 |date=March 4, 2026}}</ref> On March 5, ''[[The Atlantic]]'' reported that Trump advisers expected the president to endorse Cornyn in the runoff election after his unexpectedly strong performance in the first round of voting.<ref name="atlantic1">{{cite web |last1=Parker |first1=Ashley |title=Trump Is Expected to Endorse Cornyn |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/politics/2026/03/trump-cornyn-endorsement-texas/686232/ |website=The Atlantic |access-date=March 5, 2026 |language=en |date=March 4, 2026}}</ref>

=== Runoff ===

==== Campaign ====
Political observers described the runoff campaign between Paxton and Cornyn as "vile" and "brutal", featuring almost exclusively negative advertising from both sides.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dallas Morning News Editorial Board |date=May 12, 2026 |title=The vile unreality of Ken Paxton, John Cornyn, Mayes Middleton and Chip Roy |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/opinion/editorials/article/vile-unreality-paxton-cornyn-middleton-roy-22253446.php |access-date=May 12, 2026 |website=Dallas News |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":8">{{Cite web |last=Guo |first=Kayla |date=May 14, 2026 |title=Cornyn and Paxton go scorched earth in Senate GOP runoff |url=https://www.texastribune.org/2026/05/14/texas-us-senate-gop-runoff-cornyn-paxton-attack-ads-spending/ |access-date=May 14, 2026 |website=The Texas Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref> Cornyn repeatedly attacked Paxton's character, especially regarding alleged [[infidelity]] towards his wife, state senator [[Angela Paxton]], who had filed for divorce on "biblical grounds", and compared his ethics to that of a "strip club owner."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Morton |first=Joseph |date=May 8, 2026 |title=John Cornyn campaign has sharp Mother's Day message for Ken Paxton |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/news/politics/article/john-cornyn-sends-ken-paxton-mother-s-day-22249024.php |access-date=May 12, 2026 |website=Dallas News |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":7">{{Cite web |last=Zimmermann |first=David |date=May 8, 2026 |title=Cornyn compares Paxton's ethics to a strip club owner's |url=https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/campaigns/congressional/4561007/texas-senate-primary-cornyn-paxton-strip-club/ |access-date=May 12, 2026 |website=Washington Examiner |language=en-US}}</ref> He also highlighted the political scandals that have plagued Paxton's career, including his [[Ken Paxton#Texas House investigation and impeachment|2023 impeachment]] by the [[Texas House of Representatives]], framing him as corrupt and unfit for political office.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Solomon |first=Dan |date=May 11, 2026 |title=John Cornyn's Inexplicably Deep-Lore Campaign Against Ken Paxton |url=https://www.texasmonthly.com/news-politics/john-cornyn-obscure-campaign-ken-paxton/ |access-date=May 12, 2026 |website=The Texan}}</ref> Paxton continued to frame Cornyn as insufficiently loyal to Donald Trump.<ref name=":7" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Dearman |first=Eleanor |date=April 24, 2026 |title=Sen. John Cornyn is 'not a Trump guy,' AG Ken Paxton tells Grapevine Republicans |url=https://www.star-telegram.com/news/politics-government/state-politics/article315516064.html |access-date=May 12, 2026 |website=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]]}}</ref> His office also drew scrutiny over a sharp increase in publicly-announced lawsuits made in his capacity as [[Texas Attorney General|attorney general]] since announcing his Senate run and especially in the months immediately before the March primary. A sizeable number of these actions focused on issues salient to conservative voters, including [[Immigration policy in Texas|immigration]], [[Islam]], [[DEI]], [[student protest]]s, and elections, drawing accusations that he used his office to energize his voter base and boost his campaign ahead of the runoff.<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Brooks Harper|first1=Karen|last2=Jankowski|first2=Philip |date=May 14, 2026 |title=As Cornyn-Paxton race heats up, AG's public investigations surge |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/news/politics/article/cornyn-paxton-senate-race-heats-up-ag-public-22253455.php |access-date=May 20, 2026 |website=Dallas News |language=en}}</ref>

The runoff significantly fractured both the Republican electorate and officeholders in the state, many of whom worried that the money spent and political attacks exchanged during the contest could benefit Democratic nominee [[James Talarico]]. Talarico won his primary outright, avoiding a runoff and allowing him to shift his focus to the general election early.<ref name=":8" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Moritz |first=John C. |date=May 10, 2026 |title=From Hallmark to hardball: John Cornyn and Ken Paxton go scorched earth |url=https://www.statesman.com/news/columns/article/texas-senate-paxton-cornyn-republican-runoff-22249941.php |access-date=May 12, 2026 |website=Austin American-Statesman |language=en}}</ref> [[Lieutenant Governor of Texas|Lieutenant governor]] [[Dan Patrick (politician)|Dan Patrick]] even warned that a depressed Republican turnout could jeopardize Republican control of the Texas House, though most others dismissed that as extremely unlikely, with many Republicans still expressing confidence that both Paxton and Cornyn could win the general election.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Serrano |first=Alejandro |date=April 8, 2026 |title=Dan Patrick says GOP will have "tough time" holding Texas House |url=https://www.texastribune.org/2026/04/08/texas-house-dan-patrick-gop-majority-2026-midterms-cornyn-paxton/ |access-date=May 12, 2026 |website=The Texas Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Svitek |first=Patrick |date=April 30, 2026 |title='It's a mess': With no Trump endorsement in Texas Senate race, Cornyn and Paxton are locked in an expensive brawl |url=https://www.cnn.com/2026/04/30/politics/texas-senate-runoff-john-cornyn-ken-paxton-donald-trump |access-date=May 20, 2026 |website=CNN |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last1=James |first1=Julia |last2=Jankowski |first2=Philip |date=May 4, 2026 |title=Texas House fight likely narrows to few districts despite chatter of shakeup this year |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/news/politics/article/control-texas-house-likely-narrows-districts-22230082.php |access-date=May 20, 2026 |website=Dallas News |language=en}}</ref>

Despite speculation following his first-place primary finish that Trump would endorse Cornyn, Trump did not endorse either candidate by the March 17 withdrawal deadline. Republicans had hoped the non-endorsed candidate would exit to avoid a costly runoff and allow the nominee to focus on the general election. However, Paxton refused to withdraw unless the Senate eliminated the [[filibuster]] to pass the [[SAVE America Act]]. Meanwhile, Cornyn, previously a staunch defender of the filibuster, signaled openness to reforming or bypassing it, as Trump indicated his endorsement could hinge on the bill's passage.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Birenbaum |first=Gabby |date=March 17, 2026 |title=Cornyn, Paxton locked in for runoff ballot after deadline |url=https://www.texastribune.org/2026/03/17/texas-senate-gop-primary-runoff-deadline-remove-name-from-ballot-cornyn-paxton/ |access-date=March 18, 2026 |website=The Texas Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Diamante |first=Reena |date=March 18, 2026 |title=Cornyn reconsiders Senate filibuster as he and Paxton stay in runoff race |url=https://spectrumlocalnews.com/tx/south-texas-el-paso/news/2026/03/18/texas-senate-gop-primary-runoff-filibuster- |access-date=March 18, 2026 |website=spectrumlocalnews.com |language=en}}</ref> Both candidates continued to court Trump's endorsement to consolidate support from the party, but Trump remained neutral in the race over two months after initially signaling his intention to endorse one of them.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schwager |first=Adam |date=May 9, 2026 |title=Trump on endorsing Cornyn or Paxton in Texas Senate runoff: 'I'll make a decision' |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/nexstar_media_wire/5870665-trump-on-endorsing-cornyn-or-paxton-in-texas-senate-runoff-ill-make-a-decision/?tbref=hp |access-date=May 12, 2026 |website=The Hill}}</ref> This jockeying included policy-related moves as well as superficial ones, such as a bill introduced by Cornyn to designate [[U.S. Route 287]] as Interstate 47 to honor Trump.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ardary |first=Steven |date=May 12, 2026 |title=Cornyn moves to honor Trump with Highway 287 renaming bill |url=https://www.fox26houston.com/news/cornyn-trump-interstate-highway-287 |access-date=May 14, 2026 |website=FOX 26 |language=en-US}}</ref>

On May 19, one week before the runoff, Trump announced his endorsement of Ken Paxton.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowman |first=Bridget |date=May 19, 2026 |title=Trump endorses Ken Paxton over Sen. John Cornyn ahead of Texas Republican Senate runoff |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/trump-endorses-ken-paxton-sen-john-cornyn-ahead-texas-republican-senat-rcna345898 |access-date=May 19, 2026 |website=[[NBC News]] |language=en-US}}</ref> U.S. representative [[Wesley Hunt]], who finished third in the first round of the primary, also endorsed Paxton that day.<ref name="Hunt"/>

Following the runoff, Cornyn indicated tacit support for Paxton, saying he would vote for him and would back the Republican ticket but would not actively campaign for him.<ref name=Cornyn>{{Cite web |last=Touchberry |first=Ramsey |date=June 9, 2026 |title=Cornyn says he won't campaign for Paxton in Texas Senate race |url=https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/campaigns/congressional/4601401/cornyn-paxton-texas-senate-campaign-talarico/ |access-date=June 11, 2026 |website=Washington Examiner |language=en-US}}</ref>

Paxton defeated Cornyn with 64% of the runoff vote, becoming the first challenger to defeat an incumbent senator in a primary election in the state since [[Lloyd Bentsen]] defeated [[Ralph Yarborough]] in [[1970 United States Senate election in Texas|1970]].<ref name=":9">{{Cite web |last1=Martinez |first1=Alejandra |last2=Guo |first2=Kayla |last3=Birenbaum |first3=Gabby |date=May 27, 2026 |title=Ken Paxton defeats John Cornyn in Texas U.S. Senate GOP runoff |url=https://www.texastribune.org/2026/05/26/texas-john-cornyn-ken-paxton-us-senate-republican-primary-runoff/ |access-date=May 30, 2026 |website=The Texas Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref> Cornyn became the second senator in the [[2026 United States Senate elections|2026 election cycle]] to lose renomination, after [[Bill Cassidy]] in [[2026 United States Senate election in Louisiana|Louisiana]]. His loss largely mirrored Cassidy's, performing best in the state's most Democratic-leaning areas, as well as wealthier suburban areas. Excluding sparsely populated [[Kenedy County, Texas|Kenedy County]], Cornyn only won [[Travis County, Texas|Travis County]], home to the state capital [[Austin, Texas|Austin]], a heavily left-leaning area, while narrowly losing [[Dallas County, Texas|Dallas County]], home to the wealthy [[Park Cities, Texas|Park Cities]] and [[Southern Methodist University]].<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Coleman |first1=J. Miles |last2=Kondik |first2=Kyle |date=May 27, 2026 |title=Texas Senate to Leans Republican Following Paxton Win; TX-35 Makes Same Move; Redistricting Updates |url=https://centerforpolitics.org/crystalball/texas-senate-to-leans-republican-following-paxton-win-tx-35-makes-same-move-redistricting-updates/ |access-date=May 30, 2026 |website=Sabato's Crystal Ball |language=en-US}}</ref> Paxton's runoff performance was the largest for a second-place finisher in a U.S. Senate primary in Texas, eclipsing [[Charles A. Culberson]]'s previous record in [[1916 United States Senate election in Texas|1916]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ostermeier |first=Eric |date=May 27, 2026 |title=Ken Paxton and a Review of Texas US Senate Primary Runoffs |url=https://smartpolitics.lib.umn.edu/2026/05/27/ken-paxton-and-a-review-of-texas-us-senate-primary-runoffs/ |access-date=May 31, 2026 |website=Smart Politics |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Democratic primary==
[[File:Rep. Jasmine Crockett - 118th Congress (cropped 3x4).jpg|thumb|170x170px|[[U.S. Representative]] [[Jasmine Crockett]] finished second in the Democratic primary.]]

=== Background ===
Democrats, who have not won a statewide election in Texas since [[1994 Texas lieutenant gubernatorial election|1994]], see an opening in the state due to the bitter and divisive primary fight in the Republican side, a potential midterm backlash against the [[Second Trump presidency|Trump administration]], negative approval ratings for President Trump in Texas, as well as recent polling numbers showing competitive matchups.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.ktsm.com/news/texas-politics/state-of-texas-republicans-announce-campaigns-democrats-plot-strategy-for-2026/ | title=State of Texas: Republicans announce campaigns, Democrats plot strategy for 2026 | work=KTSM 9 News | date=June 28, 2025 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=June 27, 2025 |title=Democrats Allred, Castro, O'Rourke, Talarico meet to discuss 2026 options |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/news/politics/2025/06/26/democrats-allred-castro-orourke-talarico-meet-to-discuss-2026-options/ |access-date=June 29, 2025 |website=Dallas News |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=June 26, 2025 |title=Donald Trump's approval rating goes negative in Texas |url=https://www.newsweek.com/donald-trump-approval-rating-negative-texas-2091135 |access-date=June 29, 2025 |website=Newsweek |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Guo |first=Kayla |date=June 16, 2025 |title=Here are some of the Texas Democrats eyeing statewide runs in 2026 |url=https://www.texastribune.org/2025/06/16/texas-democrats-candidates-2026-midterms-senate-governor/ |access-date=June 29, 2025 |website=The Texas Tribune |language=en}}</ref>

[[Colin Allred]], who unsuccessfully ran against incumbent Republican senator [[Ted Cruz]] in [[2024 United States Senate election in Texas|2024]], exited the race on December 8, 2025, which precipitated [[Jasmine Crockett]]'s entry into the race.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fields |first=Ashleigh |date=December 9, 2025 |title=Allred says he dropped Senate bid after 'professional, friendly conversation' with Crockett  |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5640369-allred-crockett-texas-congressional-race/ |access-date=December 9, 2025 |website=The Hill |language=en}}</ref>

=== Campaign ===
[[File:¡Viva_Democracy!_Awesome_turnout_last_night_at_the_James_Talarico_Rally_at_The_Backyard.jpg|thumb|A Talarico rally at The Backyard in [[San Antonio]]]]

Crockett entered the race with high name recognition and strong polling numbers, but her launch on the last day to file meant she had limited time for campaigning statewide.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Guo |first=Kayla |date=December 12, 2025 |title=Crockett leads Talarico in first head-to-head Senate poll |url=https://www.texastribune.org/2025/12/12/texas-senate-democratic-primary-poll-jasmine-crockett-james-talarico/ |access-date=April 28, 2026 |website=The Texas Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref> According to polling data in February 2026 prior to the primaries, Crockett originally had a favorability percentage of 23%, and an unfavorable percentage of 25% while Talarico came in at 18% favorable and 9% unfavorable.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 23, 2026 |title=Jasmine Crockett Favorability (February 2026) |url=https://texaspolitics.utexas.edu/set/jasmine-crockett-favorability-february-2026 |access-date=April 28, 2026 |website=The Texas Politics Project |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=February 23, 2026 |title=James Talarico Favorability (February 2026) |url=https://texaspolitics.utexas.edu/set/james-talarico-favorability-february-2026 |access-date=April 28, 2026 |website=The Texas Politics Project |language=en}}</ref> She did not hire a [[campaign manager]], and focused on advertising over a staffed [[Canvassing|field operation]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Guo |first=Kayla |date=March 6, 2026 |title=Why Jasmine Crockett lost the Dem primary to James Talarico |url=https://www.texastribune.org/2026/03/06/jasmine-crockett-texas-james-talarico-democrat-us-senate-primary/ |access-date=March 22, 2026 |website=The Texas Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref>

Crockett and Talarico participated in a debate on January 24, 2026, hosted by the [[AFL-CIO]] in [[Georgetown, Texas|Georgetown]]. During the debate, both candidates largely aligned on policy and engaged in limited direct attacks. Crockett defended her "firebrand" style as necessary for the political moment, while Talarico emphasized a more measured approach and his perceived electability against Ken Paxton.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Mueller |first=Julia |date=January 24, 2026 |title=5 takeaways from the Texas Senate debate between Crockett, Talarico |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5704882-texas-senate-democrats-debate/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260126025423/https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5704882-texas-senate-democrats-debate/ |archive-date=January 26, 2026 |access-date=January 27, 2026 |work=The Hill |language=en-US}}</ref> Talarico later faced controversy after a social media influencer alleged he had referred to former rival Colin Allred as a "mediocre Black man" in comparison to Crockett in a private conversation; Talarico disputed the claim as a mischaracterization. Allred subsequently endorsed Crockett and criticized Talarico.<ref name="auto" /> The episode further exposed the racial tension between each candidate's base of support, with Crockett performing best among [[African Americans|Black]] voters, Democrats' strongest voter base, and Talarico performing best among [[White Americans|White]] and [[Hispanic and Latino Americans|Latino]] voters, demographics which hold far more [[swing vote]]rs.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowman |first=Bridget |date=February 5, 2026 |title=Viral dispute over 'mediocre' comment exposes racial divides in Democrats' Texas Senate primary |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/viral-dispute-mediocre-comment-exposes-racial-divides-democrats-texas-rcna257284 |access-date=February 5, 2026 |website=NBC News |language=en}}</ref>

On February 16, Talarico was scheduled to appear on ''[[The Late Show with Stephen Colbert]]''. According to Colbert, however, [[CBS]] did not allow him to air the interview nor mention the cancellation on-air based on a recently revised interpretation of the [[Federal Communications Commission|FCC]]'s [[equal-time rule]], although he did discuss it during that night's episode in spite of FCC threats. Colbert later posted the interview to the show's [[YouTube]] page.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Moorman |first=Taijuan |title=Colbert slams CBS for canning interview with Trump critic |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/entertainment/tv/2026/02/17/colbert-james-talarico-cbs-interview-trump/88715400007/ |access-date=February 17, 2026 |website=USA TODAY |language=en-US}}</ref> The interview gained millions of views online, while Talarico fundraised $2.5 million in the aftermath and increased his name recognition as [[early voting]] began ahead of the March 3 primary. Analysts largely viewed the campaign as one based on personality and electability rather than ideology.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mueller |first=Julia |date=February 19, 2026 |title=Talarico gets burst of momentum from CBS controversy |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5744369-cbs-late-show-controversy/ |access-date=February 21, 2026 |website=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]]}}</ref>

After the primary, Crockett conceded to Talarico,<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 4, 2026|title=Crockett, after warning of disenfranchisement, concedes to Talarico in Texas Senate race|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/03/04/crockett-voting-confusion-dallas-texas-00811419|access-date=April 27, 2026|website=Politico|language=en}}</ref> announcing support for his candidacy, but she declined to actively campaign for him.<ref name="Rahman">{{cite web|last=Rahman|first=Yasira|date=March 5, 2026|title=Jasmine Crockett backs James Talarico after loss but won't 'make plans' to campaign for fellow Dem|url=https://news.meaww.com/jasmine-crockett-backs-james-talarico-after-loss-but-wont-make-plans-to-campaign-for-fellow-dem|website=MEAWW|access-date=May 31, 2026}}</ref>
