James Talarico won the Democratic primary with 52.4% of the vote.<ref name="primary-results-nyt">{{cite news|author1=NYT Election Results Team |title=Texas U.S. Senate Primary Election Results |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2026/us/elections/results-texas-us-senate-primary.html |access-date=March 4, 2026|work=[[The New York Times]] |date=March 4, 2026}}</ref> After a dispute concerning voting hours in [[Dallas County, Texas|Dallas]] and [[Williamson County, Texas|Williamson Counties]] on the night of the primary, Crockett conceded the race on March 4.<ref name="crockett-resign">{{cite news |last1=Howard |first1=Andrew |last2=Crampton |first2=Liz |title=Crockett, after warning of disenfranchisement, concedes to Talarico in Texas Senate race |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/03/04/crockett-voting-confusion-dallas-texas-00811419 |access-date=March 4, 2026 |work=Politico |date=March 4, 2026}}</ref> The dispute in Dallas County arose from the county Republican Party's decision not to use countywide voting centers, where voters can cast ballots at any location, on Election Day, as Texas law requires both parties to agree in order to implement them.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Votebeat |date=March 4, 2026 |title=Dallas County voters frustrated over precinct-based primary |url=https://dallasfreepress.com/west-dallas/dallas-county-precinct-voting-problems-jasmine-crockett-james-talarico-democrats-gop/ |access-date=March 17, 2026 |website=The Texas Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref> On March 17, the Dallas County GOP announced it would use countywide voting centers for the runoff.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Contreras |first=Natalia |date=March 17, 2026 |title=Dallas GOP will OK countywide voting sites for May 26 runoff |url=https://www.texastribune.org/2026/03/17/dallas-county-republican-party-voting-sites-primary-runoff/ |access-date=March 17, 2026 |website=The Texas Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref>

Issues with a ballot scanning and tabulation machine in [[Newton County, Texas|Newton County]] led to the county clerk writing in a court filing that its Democratic statewide primary results, with Hassan winning the county, were "skewed" and that a recount was required, which eventually had to be done by hand due to the scanning issues persisting,<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 10, 2026 |title=Texas county starts election recount after "ballot coding error" leads to "skewed" results |url=https://abc13.com/post/texas-county-starts-election-recount-ballot-coding-error-leads-skewed-results/18697268/ |access-date=March 12, 2026 |website=ABC13 Houston |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=March 10, 2026 |title=Officials may have to have hand count votes after Newton County recount fails electronically |url=https://abc13.com/post/officials-may-have-hand-count-votes-newton-county-recount-fails-electronically/18700356/ |access-date=March 12, 2026 |website=ABC13 Houston |language=en}}</ref> with the revised results showing Crockett winning the county.

Democrats cast more primary votes in a midterm election than Republicans for the first time since [[2002 United States Senate election in Texas|2002]].<ref name=":6" /> The results largely mirrored those of the [[2020 United States Senate election in Texas#Democratic primary|2020 primary for this seat]], which also pitted a Black Democrat from Dallas ([[Royce West]]) against a White Democrat from the [[Austin, Texas|Austin]] area ([[M. J. Hegar]]). Crockett performed best among Black voters, winning by large margins in [[East Texas]], as well as by smaller margins in the urban centers of Dallas and [[Harris County, Texas|Harris]] counties. Talarico won the White and [[Hispanic and Latino Americans|Hispanic]] vote, dominating in the Austin metro area, and winning the state's remaining rural areas, including the heavily-Hispanic [[Rio Grande Valley]].<ref name=":5" />

== Libertarian convention ==
The [[Libertarian Party (United States)|Libertarian Party]] convention was held from April 10 to 12, 2026, in [[Abilene, Texas|Abilene]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2026 Libertarian Party Convention |url=https://2026.lptexas.org/ |access-date=March 24, 2026 |website=2026 Convention |language=en}}</ref> Ted Brown, the party's U.S. senate nominee in [[2024 United States Senate election in Texas|2024]], secured the nomination with 83 votes to Daniel "Mark" Sims's 39.<ref name="BLib">{{cite web |title=United States Senate election in Texas, 2026 |url=https://ballotpedia.org/United_States_Senate_election_in_Texas,_2026 |website=Ballotpedia |access-date=April 17, 2026 |language=en |date=March 4, 2026}}</ref>
== General election ==

=== Campaign ===
Following the May Republican runoff, both nominees quickly pivoted to the general election.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zurcher |first=Anthony |date=May 27, 2026 |title=Ken Paxton's win over John Cornyn in Texas primary may also help Democrats in Senate battle |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/clypprglrlyo |access-date=June 11, 2026 |website=BBC News |language=en-GB}}</ref> Paxton's victory was welcomed by Democrats who viewed him as a weaker opponent, leading several nonpartisan forecasters to rate the race as more competitive.<ref name=":9" /> Talarico adopted a more aggressive strategy, highlighting allegations that led to Paxton's impeachment by fellow Republicans.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 28, 2026 |title=Talarico targets Paxton's scandals in Texas Senate race, pivoting from his sunny primary message |url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/talarico-targets-paxtons-scandals-in-texas-senate-race-pivoting-from-his-sunny-primary-message |access-date=June 11, 2026 |website=PBS}}</ref>

==== Economy ====
Both Talarico and Paxton launched campaigns related to economic issues: Talarico's economic plan is named the "''New American Dream,''" while Paxton's is named "''Protecting the Texas Promise''".<ref name="Website-1">{{Cite web |last=Guo |first=Kayla |date=August 5, 2026 |title=James Talarico rolls out economic agenda that takes aim at “false Gospel of trickle-down economics” |url=https://www.texastribune.org/2026/08/05/texas-senate-james-talarico-economic-agenda-ken-paxton/ |access-date=October 22, 2026 |website=[[The Texas Tribune]]}}</ref> Talarico supports raising [[Minimum wage in the United States|the minimum wage]], canceling medical debt, and passing universal [[Child care|childcare]] and [[Parental leave|paid family leave]].<ref name="Website-1" /> Paxton supports [[Tax deduction|tax deductions]] for [[Healthcare in the United States|healthcare]], [[Housing in the United States|housing]], and family-related expenses.<ref name="Website-1" />

==== Social and legal issues ====
Paxton portrayed Talarico as an extremist, emphasizing [[culture war]] issues and [[gender]], while criticizing his statement that "[[God]] is [[non-binary]]" and questioning his [[masculinity]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowman |first=Bridget |date=May 27, 2026 |title=Ken Paxton defeats GOP Sen. John Cornyn in Texas primary runoff |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/texas-runoff-primary-election-winner-paxton-trump-cornyn-rcna346552 |access-date=June 11, 2026 |website=NBC News |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Kurtzleben |first=Danielle |date=May 30, 2026 |title=What it means to be a man is a theme in Texas Senate race as Paxton attacks Talarico |url=https://www.npr.org/2026/05/30/nx-s1-5839468/texas-senate-talarico-paxton-gender-masculinity |access-date=June 11, 2026 |work=NPR |language=en}}</ref> Paxton also repeatedly called Talarico a vegan, claiming "you can't get elected as a vegan in Texas," prompting Talarico to release photos and videos of himself eating meat and other non-vegan foods at campaign events.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.politifact.com/factchecks/2026/may/27/ken-paxton/in-texas-senate-race-ken-paxton-falsely-claims-jam/|title= Democratic Texas U.S. Senate candidate James Talarico "is a vegan."|work=PolitiFact|date=May 26, 2026}}</ref> In June, Talarico criticized the Attorney General's office over its handling of a child sexual abuse case involving former attorney Adam Hoffman during Paxton's tenure.<ref name=":10">{{Cite news |last=McGaughy |first=Lauren |date=June 18, 2026 |title=James Talarico Attacks Ken Paxton Over Handling of Child Sex Abuse Case |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/18/us/talarico-paxton-child-sex-abuse-case.html |access-date=June 23, 2026 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US}}</ref> After a mistrial, Hoffman received a plea deal critics called "unusually lenient" and an "[[Jeffrey Epstein|Epstein]]-style sweetheart deal," as it did not require him to register as a sex offender.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Sitz |first1=Alicia |last2=Carter |first2=Tatiana |date=June 8, 2026 |title=As Paxton heads to Senate race, critics revisit child sex abuse plea deal |url=https://www.newsnationnow.com/crime/paxton-senate-sex-abuse-plea-deal/ |website=NewsNation}}</ref> Talarico and John Cornyn had previously aired campaign ads criticizing Paxton over the case.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Powell |first=Adam |title=Cornyn keeps up attacks on Paxton in Texas US Senate runoff |url=https://www.elpasotimes.com/story/news/politics/elections/2026/05/07/cornyn-targets-paxton-over-plea-deal-for-sex-abuser-in-texas-us-senate-race/89977335007/ |access-date=June 23, 2026 |website=El Paso Times |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Guo |first=Kayla |date=May 27, 2026 |url=https://www.texastribune.org/2026/05/27/james-talarico-ken-paxton-launch-attack-ads-in-texas-u-s-senate-race/ |title=Tala-freak-o vs. Ken the Criminal: Texas candidates sharpen attacks as U.S. Senate race locks in |work=[[The Texas Tribune]] |access-date=September 20, 2026}}</ref>

==== Party unification ====
Both Talarico and Paxton have faced challenges unifying their parties after the primaries, with limited support from former rivals exposing weaknesses in their coalitions.<ref name=":11">{{Cite web |last=Guo |first=Kayla |date=June 24, 2026 |title=Cornyn, Crockett loom large in Senate race after primary losses |url=https://www.texastribune.org/2026/06/24/john-cornyn-jasmine-crockett-talarico-paxton-texas-senate/ |access-date=July 9, 2026 |website=[[The Texas Tribune]] |language=en-US}}</ref> Talarico has sought to bolster support among Black voters after defeating Jasmine Crockett, who skipped the state Democratic convention and declined to commit to campaigning for him, raising concerns about Black turnout.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Guo |first=Kayla |date=June 27, 2026 |title=Talarico looks for momentum with Black voters at Dem convention |url=https://www.texastribune.org/2026/06/27/texas-democratic-convention-james-talarico-black-voters-jasmine-crockett/ |access-date=July 9, 2026 |website=The Texas Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref> Paxton has struggled with moderate Republicans who backed John Cornyn, with polls showing some Cornyn voters supporting Talarico.<ref name=":11" /> Cornyn has also declined to fundraise for Paxton, instead focusing on competitive [[2026 United States Senate elections|Senate races in other states]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Birenbaum |first=Gabby |date=August 28, 2026 |title=Why John Cornyn won't be fundraising in Texas' U.S. Senate race |url=https://www.texastribune.org/2026/08/28/john-cornyn-ken-paxton-texas-fundraising-talarico-senate-race/ |access-date=August 28, 2026 |website=The Texas Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref> 

In part to rally support behind candidates such as Paxton, the Republican Party hosted its first-ever [[2026 Republican National Convention|midterm national convention]] in [[Dallas]] on September 9 and 10.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ardary |first=Steven |date=September 2, 2026 |title=Trump says Dallas GOP midterm convention will be 'big stuff' |url=https://www.fox4news.com/news/trump-dallas-gop-midterm-convention-paxton-talarico |access-date=September 4, 2026 |website=FOX Local |publisher=FOX 4 News Dallas-Fort Worth |language=en-US}}</ref> After the midterm convention, Paxton said in a private conversation that the convention had a negative effect for the Republican Party.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mediaite.com/media/news/bombshell-leaked-audio-shows-ken-paxton-dissing-trumps-convention-blaming-it-for-his-bad-polls-everybodys-numbers-dropped/|title=Bombshell Leaked Audio Shows Ken Paxton Dissing Trump's Convention — Blaming It for His Bad Polls: 'Everybody's Numbers Dropped'|work=Mediaite|date=September 30, 2026|last=Durante |first=Tom|access-date =September 30, 2026}}</ref>

==== Attempts of holding debate ====
On July 16, the Paxton and Talarico campaigns announced negotiations for up to three general election debates.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Whitely |first=Jason |date=July 16, 2026 |title=Talarico says yes to three debates. Paxton's response: 'Of course we are going to debate.' |url=https://www.wfaa.com/article/news/local/talarico-says-yes-three-debates-paxton/287-4b91cce7-20e7-49af-a119-72efe369990b |website=WFAA}}</ref> If held, they would mark Paxton's first debates since becoming a statewide elected official.<ref>{{Cite news |last=McGaughy |first=Lauren |date=July 16, 2026 |title=Paxton Agrees to Debate Talarico in Texas Senate Race |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/07/16/us/paxton-talarico-debate-texas-senate.html |access-date=July 20, 2026 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Birenbaum |first=Gabby |date=July 16, 2026 |title=Ken Paxton says he'll debate James Talarico in Texas Senate race |url=https://www.texastribune.org/2026/07/16/texas-ken-paxton-james-talarico-debate-senate-race-2026/ |access-date=July 20, 2026 |website=The Texas Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Barragán |first=James |date=February 24, 2022 |title=Debate between Texas GOP attorney general candidates got heated, even though incumbent Ken Paxton wasn't there |url=https://www.texastribune.org/?p=109993 |access-date=July 20, 2026 |website=The Texas Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref> By September, Talarico had accepted a fourth invitation to a debate as Paxton had remained noncommittal, but insisted that they were still negotiating and expected to participate in at least one debate before the election.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bugenhagen |first=Faith |date=September 2, 2026 |title=Talarico accepts debate invitation; Paxton criticizes event but doesn't commit |url=https://www.statesman.com/news/politics/state/article/talarico-paxton-cnn-texas-senate-debate-22414048.php |access-date=September 18, 2026 |website=Austin American-Statesman |language=en}}</ref> Responding to a challenge issued by Talarico to appear on the channel,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Guo|first=Kayla |date=September 24, 2026 |title=James Talarico challenges Ken Paxton to Fox News debate |url=https://www.texastribune.org/2026/09/24/james-talarico-tribfest-2026/ |access-date=October 5, 2026 |website=The Texas Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref> a fifth debate invitation was issued by [[Fox News]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Murray |first=Casey |date=September 29, 2026 |title=Fox News will host Texas Senate debate if Ken Paxton agrees to face off|url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/politics/texas/article/paxton-talarico-debate-22455301.php |access-date=October 5, 2026 |website=Houston Chronicle |language=en}}</ref> In early October, president Donald Trump and several other prominent Republicans called on Paxton to debate Talarico.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rahman |first=Khaleda |date=October 9, 2026 |title=Ken Paxton Avoided Debates for Years. Now He May Have No Choice |url=https://www.newsweek.com/ken-paxton-avoided-debates-years-may-have-no-choice-12540874 |access-date=October 11, 2026 |website=Newsweek |language=en}}</ref> {{As of|2026|October|18|df=US}}, Paxton has not accepted an invitation to a single debate with Talarico.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Manchester |first=Julia |last2=Mueller |first2=Julia |date=October 18, 2026 |title=With Ken Paxton's race faltering, GOP looks for someone to blame |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/6155048-ken-paxton-republicans-texas-senate-race-trump/ |work=The Hill}}</ref> If no debate is held, it would mark the first Senate race in Texas since [[2000 United States Senate election in Texas|2000]] not to feature a debate between the major party candidates.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Guo |first=Kayla |date=October 7, 2026 |title=Texas Republicans are refusing to debate for the election |url=https://www.texastribune.org/2026/10/07/texas-debate-republicans-talarico-paxton-abbott-hinojosa-election/ |access-date=October 26, 2026 |work=[[The Texas Tribune]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Election administration ===
The election is taking place amidst a broader push by the Trump administration to restrict [[Postal voting in the United States|mail-in voting]], although these efforts are currently mired in court proceedings.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gilani |first=Haajrah |date=September 2, 2026 |title=What the US Postal Service's effort to reshape mail-in voting means for Texas |url=https://www.expressnews.com/politics/article/usps-mail-voting-texas-22412931.php |access-date=September 4, 2026 |website=San Antonio Express-News |language=en}}</ref> On September 1, commissioners in [[Tarrant County]], Texas's third-largest county, voted to close roughly a third of its polling locations, a year after cutting early-voting sites in half, citing cost savings at low-turnout locations. Critics warned the closures could increase travel times and suppress turnout.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Zaru |first=Deena |title=Amid public outcry, Tarrant County, Texas cuts polling locations ahead of 2026 midterm elections |url=https://abcnews.com/Politics/amid-public-outcry-tarrant-county-texas-cuts-polling/story?id=136116581 |work=ABC News |date=September 1, 2026 |access-date=September 2, 2026}}</ref> Later that month, [[Votebeat]] reported that the [[Texas Department of Public Safety|Department of Public Safety]] had failed to distribute nearly 200,000 voter registrations to counties over the course of the past year due to a technical error, sparking a bipartisan outcry.<ref name=":2" /> By the beginning of October, the reported size of the backlog had neared 600,000 registrations.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=McManus |first1=Tracey |last2=Tong |first2=William |date=October 2, 2026 |title=Map: Texas DPS voter registrations backlog tracker |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/projects/2026/texas-voter-registration-backlog-tracker/ |access-date=October 4, 2026 |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |language=en}}</ref> The backlog was sent to counties all at once, with many of the state's urban counties receiving tens of thousands one month before [[early voting]] was set to begin.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last1=DeGuzman |first1=Colleen |last2=Contreras |first2=Natalia |date=September 24, 2026 |title=GOP official: Texas should have caught voter registration error |url=https://www.votebeat.org/texas/2026/06/24/team-voter-registration-system-civix-secretary-of-state/ |access-date=September 29, 2026 |website=The Texas Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref> The state agreed to reimburse counties for the [[overtime]] pay incurred processing the glut of applications.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Behrndt |first=Rachel |date=September 29, 2026 |title=State agrees to pay counties as they work to clear voter registration backlog |url=https://www.wfaa.com/article/news/politics/elections/texas-voter-registration-back-log-funding-glitch-error-pays/287-c61b041d-f622-498d-b971-33838bb88182 |access-date=September 29, 2026 |work=WFAA}}</ref> Observers and election experts highlighted the debacle as an example of the difficulties involved in registering to vote in Texas, one of the only states in the country to not offer universal online voter registration.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=DeGuzman |first1=Colleen |last2=Contreras |first2=Natalia |date=September 26, 2026 |title=Texas' delayed voter applications highlight registration woes |url=https://www.votebeat.org/texas/2026/09/26/voter-registration-delay-backlog-online-dps-error/ |access-date=October 4, 2026 |website=The Texas Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Fundraising===
Talarico has considerably outraised Paxton throughout the campaign. Due to the high national profile of the race, both candidates, especially Talarico have received significant contributions from voters across the country. Within Texas, Talarico's donation base is concentrated in his home city of [[Austin, Texas|Austin]] and the state's other urban areas, while Paxton's is in [[Dallas]].<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Quinton |first1=Phoebe |last2=Moritz |first2=John C. |date=September 29, 2026 |title=The money behind Talarico and Paxton's Senate race, mapped by ZIP code |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/projects/2026/talarico-paxton-donations-map/ |access-date=October 1, 2026 |website=Dallas Morning News |language=en}}</ref> The Talarico campaign raised $64 million in the third quarter of 2026, the largest quarterly total by a U.S. Senate candidate ever, surpassing the $57 million record that had been set by [[Jaime Harrison]] in the [[2020 United States Senate election in South Carolina|2020 South Carolina senate race]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 15, 2026 |title=James Talarico announces record-breaking $64M haul |url=https://www.politico.com/live-updates/2026/10/15/congress/james-talarico-64-million-fundraising-record-01119808 |access-date=October 15, 2026 |website=[[Politico]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Birenbaum |first=Gabby |date=October 15, 2026 |title=James Talarico raises record $64 million in third quarter |url=https://www.texastribune.org/2026/10/15/james-talarico-64-million-fundraising-texas-senate/ |access-date=October 15, 2026 |work=[[The Texas Tribune]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

Despite Talarico's individual fundraising advantage, however, leading into the fall campaign season, and particularly after the [[2026 Republican National Convention|Republican National Convention]] in Dallas, Paxton has seen a massive infusion of [[political action committee]] and political party spending on his behalf to try to buoy his sagging polling numbers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Howard |first=Andrew |date=September 11, 2026 |title=Republicans just opened the floodgates on spending for Ken Paxton |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/09/11/gop-money-texas-paxton-trump-01072972 |access-date=September 28, 2026|website=[[Politico]] |language=en}}</ref> The [[Senate Leadership Fund]] alone committed over $100 million to support Paxton, far exceeding Talarico's individual fundraising numbers, though a remarkably high investment to defend a seat in a state Republicans have not lost in over 30 years.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Birenbaum |first=Gabby |date=September 23, 2026 |title=Senate Republicans increase ad buy for Ken Paxton to $100M |url=https://www.texastribune.org/2026/09/22/texas-paxton-ads-100-million-senate-race-talarico/ |access-date=September 28, 2026 |website=The Texas Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref> [[Elon Musk]] also donated $10 million to Lone Star Liberty PAC, a group supporting Ken Paxton.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Elon Musk quietly becomes biggest known donor in midterm contests as he tries to save Republicans |website=[[AP News]] |url=https://apnews.com/article/elon-musk-midterms-republicans-donors-c06efc774a2e7c5d345e0d46641eb510}}</ref> The [[Supreme Court of the United States|Supreme Court]] over the summer additionally cleared the way for political parties themselves to freely coordinate advertising spending with candidates at the candidates' reduced rate, handing Republicans a monetary advantage across the country due to the Democratic Party lagging behind the Republicans in party fundraising.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Doherty |first1=Erin |last2=Kashinsky |first2=Lisa |last3=Piper |first3=Jessica |last4=Howard |first4=Andrew |title=The Supreme Court just made the DNC's fundraising woes a much bigger problem|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/06/30/the-supreme-court-just-made-the-dncs-fundraising-woes-a-much-bigger-problem-00983172 |access-date=September 28, 2026 |website=Politico |language=en}}</ref>  By October, AdImpact data cited by Reuters put pro-Paxton spending at about $239 million, against roughly $45 million from major Democratic-aligned groups. Texas PAC, a Republican super PAC, accounted for nearly $149 million of that advertising. Federal filings separately showed that Elon Musk gave $158 million to the Senate Leadership Fund, which passed an equivalent sum to Texas PAC. Lone Star Rising PAC, the largest Democratic-aligned outside group, spent $19.3 million on advertising.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Brooks |first1=Brad |last2=Sullivan |first2=Andy |last3=Somasekhar |first3=Arathy |last4=Sullivan |first4=Andy |date=October 21, 2026 |title=Republicans bet Musk’s millions can rescue Texas' Paxton in US Senate race |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/us/republicans-bet-musks-millions-can-rescue-texas-paxton-us-senate-race-2026-10-21/ |access-date=October 26, 2026 |work=Reuters |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Birenbaum |first=Gabby |last2=Serrano |first2=Alejandro |date=October 15, 2026 |title=Elon Musk gave $158 million to Senate GOP group helping Paxton |url=https://www.texastribune.org/2026/10/15/elon-musk-ken-paxton-donations-senate-gop-super-pac/ |access-date=October 26, 2026 |website=The Texas Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref>
